exponent_of_ampere.description: The exponent of ampere in a product of powers of base units.
examples:
In the equation '1 milliampere = 0.001 x ampere'

the conversionFactor for milliampere is 0.001
the exponent of ampere is 1
all other exponents are zero

Every member of a unit group containing milliampere must be a multiple of ampere.
exponent_of_ampere.title: exponent of ampere

exponent_of_bit.description: The exponent of bit in a product of powers of base units.
examples:
In the equation '1 megabit per second = 1000000 x bit per second'

the conversion factor for megabit per second is 1000000
the exponent of bit is 1
the exponent of second is -1
all other exponents are zero

Every member of a unit group containing megabit per second must be a multiple of bit per second.

In the equation 'y degrees Fahrenheit = (y + 459.6669607) x 5/9 degrees Kelvin'

the conversion offset for degree Fahrenheit is 459.6669607
the conversion factor for degree Fahrenheit is 5/9
the exponent of Kelvin is 1
all other exponents are zero

Every member of a unit group containing degree Fahrenheit will have a similar equation, with different offset or conversion factor (or both).

goes_to_place.description: Relates something to its destination place.
examples: A letter has an address indicating its destination; a segment of a delivery route terminates at a delivery location; a trail terminates at an intersection with another trail.

has_accuracy.description: Relates a magnitude to another magnitude that describes its accuracy.
examples: Temperature accurate to tenth of a degree C; length accurate to the nearest centimeter.
has_accuracy.title: has accuracy

has_addend.description: Relates an aspect to another aspect that is an additive component of it.
examples: In the equation 'profit = revenue - expenses', revenue is an addend and expenses is a subtrahend.
has_addend.title: has addend

has_address.description: Relates something to its physical or electronic address.
examples: A brick-and-mortar store has a street address; a person can be contacted electronically via an email address.

has_aspect.description: Relates a magnitude to its aspect (measurable characteristic).

has_broader.description: Relates a thing to another thing with a broader meaning.
examples: The aspect distance is broader than the aspect height.
has_broader.title: has broader

has_direct_broader.description: Relates a thing to another thing with a broader meaning, when there is no intermediate between them.
has_direct_broader.title: has direct broader

has_divisor.description: Relates a unit of measure to another unit of measure that is a divisor, or relates an aspect to another aspect that is a divisor.

has_giver.description: Relates something to the participant that provides it.

has_goal.description: Relates something to the end towards which it directs effort.

has_incumbent.description: Relates a position to the thing or person that currently holds that position.

has_magnitude.description: Relates a thing to a magnitude.

has_magnitude.title: has magnitude

has_multiplier.description: Relates a unit of measure to another unit of measure that is a factor, or relates an aspect to another aspect that is a factor.

has_navigational_parent.description: Relates a child category to a parent category in an informal (e.g., faceted) hierarchy.

has_navigational_parent.title: has navigational parent

has_participant.description: Relates something (e.g. an agreement) to things that play a role, or take part or are otherwise involved in some way.

has_participant.title: has participant

has_party.description: Relates an event, agreement, or obligation to a participating person or organization.

has_party.title: has party

has_physical_location.description: Relates something to its physical location.
has_physical_location.title: has physical location

has_recipient.description: Relates something to the participant that receives or is intended to receive it.

has_recipient.title: has recipient

has_subtrahend.description: Relates an aspect to another aspect that is a subtracted component of it.
examples: In the equation 'profit = revenue - expenses', revenue is an addend and expenses is a subtrahend.
has_subtrahend.title: has subtrahend

has_unique_broader.description: Relates a thing to a unique other thing with a broader meaning.
has_unique_broader.title: has unique broader

has_unique_navigational_parent.description: Relates a subject category to a unique parent category in an informal (e.g., faceted) hierarchy.

id_text.description: A text string that identifies an individual.

is_affected_by.description: Relates an affected thing to the source of the effect.

is_assignment_of.description: Relates an assignment to the resource it assigns.

is_assignment_to.description: Relates something (typically an assignment) to the thing the resource is assigned to, such as a project, position, organization, pay rate, or billing rate.

is_part_of.description: The relationship between a part and a whole where the part has independent existence.

conversion_offset.description:
A value used along with a conversion factor to relate a unit to its corresponding unit in the International System of Units. In the equation below, the conversion offset is 459.669607 and the conversion factor is 5/9.

y degrees Fahrenheit = (y + 459.669607) x 5/9 degrees Kelvin

To convert from Fahrenheit to Kelvin, first add the offset and then multiply by the conversion factor.

To convert from Kelvin to Fahrenheit, reverse the steps: first divide by the conversion factor and then subtract the offset.

exponent_of_steradian.description: The exponent of steradian in a product of powers of base units.
examples:
In the equation '1 watt per square meter steradian = 1 x kilogram per secondCubed steradian'

the conversion factor for watt per square meter steradian is 1
the exponent of kilogram is 1
the exponent of second is -3
the exponent of steradian is -1
all other exponents are zero

Every member of a unit group containing watt per square meter steradian must a multiple of kilogram per secondCubed steradian.
exponent_of_steradian.title: exponent of steradian

exponent_of_us_dollar.description: The exponent of US Dollar in a product of powers of base units.
examples:
In the equation '1 million dollars per week = 1.65344 x dollar per second'

the conversion factor for million dollars per week is 1.65344
the exponent of US Dollar is 1
the exponent of second is -1
all other exponents are zero

Every member of a unit group containing million dollars per week must be a multiple of dollar per second.
exponent_of_us_dollar.title: exponent of US dollar

goes_to_agent.description: Relates something to the agent that receives it.
examples: A package is sent to a person; a purchase order email is received by a vendor.
goes_to_agent.title: goes to agent

goes_to_place.description: Relates something to its destination place.
examples: A letter has an address indicating its destination; a segment of a delivery route terminates at a delivery location; a trail terminates at an intersection with another trail.
goes_to_place.title: goes to place

has_accuracy.description: Relates a magnitude to another magnitude that describes its accuracy.
examples: Temperature accurate to tenth of a degree C; length accurate to the nearest centimeter.
has_accuracy.title: has accuracy

has_addend.description: Relates an aspect to another aspect that is an additive component of it.
examples: In the equation 'profit = revenue - expenses', revenue is an addend and expenses is a subtrahend.
has_addend.title: has addend

has_address.description: Relates something to its physical or electronic address.
examples: A brick-and-mortar store has a street address; a person can be contacted electronically via an email address.
has_address.title: has address

has_aspect.description: Relates a magnitude to its aspect (measurable characteristic).
has_aspect.title: has aspect

has_broader.description: Relates a thing to another thing with a broader meaning.
examples: The aspect distance is broader than the aspect height.
has_broader.title: has broader

has_direct_broader.description: Relates a thing to another thing with a broader meaning, when there is no intermediate between them.
has_direct_broader.title: has direct broader

has_divisor.description: Relates a unit of measure to another unit of measure that is a divisor, or relates an aspect to another aspect that is a divisor.
examples: Miles per hour has miles as a multiplier and hour as a divisor; speed has distance as a multiplier and duration as a divisor.
has_divisor.title: has divisor

has_giver.description: Relates something to the participant that provides it.
examples: An offer is made by a giver; an obligation has a giver who is obligated to another person; a gift is presented by the giver.
has_giver.title: has giver

has_goal.description: Relates something to the end towards which it directs effort.
examples: The sales division of a company has the goal of acquiring new customers and contracts.
has_goal.title: has goal

has_incumbent.description: Relates a position to the thing or person that currently holds that position.
has_incumbent.title: has incumbent

has_magnitude.description: Relates a thing to a magnitude.
examples: A car or model of car has magnitudes for length, width, weight, average miles per gallon, etc.
has_magnitude.title: has magnitude

has_multiplier.description: Relates a unit of measure to another unit of measure that is a factor, or relates an aspect to another aspect that is a factor.
examples: Miles per hour has miles as a multiplier and hours as a divisor; speed has distance as a multiplier and duration as a divisor.
has_multiplier.title: has multiplier

has_navigational_parent.description: Relates a child category to a parent category in an informal (e.g., faceted) hierarchy.
examples: Refrigerator handles are not refrigerators, but it may be useful to represent their relationship hierarchically for a faceted UI filter.
has_navigational_parent.title: has navigational parent

has_participant.description: Relates something (e.g. an agreement) to things that play a role, or take part or are otherwise involved in some way.
examples: An event of transferring money has a participating account that receives the money.
has_participant.title: has participant

has_party.description: Relates an event, agreement, or obligation to a participating person or organization.
examples: Loan agreements have lender and borrower parties.
has_party.title: has party

has_physical_location.description: Relates something to its physical location.
has_physical_location.title: has physical location

has_recipient.description: Relates something to the participant that receives or is intended to receive it.
examples: An offer is made to a recipient; an obligation has a recipient to whom another person is obligated; a gift is bestowed upon a recipient.
has_recipient.title: has recipient

has_subtrahend.description: Relates an aspect to another aspect that is a subtracted component of it.
examples: In the equation 'profit = revenue - expenses', revenue is an addend and expenses is a subtrahend.
has_subtrahend.title: has subtrahend

has_unique_broader.description: Relates a thing to a unique other thing with a broader meaning.
has_unique_broader.title: has unique broader

has_unique_navigational_parent.description: Relates a subject category to a unique parent category in an informal (e.g., faceted) hierarchy.
has_unique_navigational_parent.title: has unique navigational parent

id_text.description: A text string that identifies an individual.
examples: The id text for a car is '4Y1SL65848Z411439'; the id text for the HR department of some company is H31415.
id_text.title: id text

is_affected_by.description: Relates an affected thing to the source of the effect.
is_affected_by.title: is affected by

is_allocated_by.description: Relates something to whomever or whatever assigns or distributes it.
examples: A U.S. Social Security number is allocated by the U.S. Social Security Administration; the media type https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/text/csv is allocated by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA).
is_allocated_by.title: is allocated by

is_assignment_of.description: Relates an assignment to the resource it assigns.
examples: Assignment of a person to a project.
is_assignment_of.title: is assignment of

is_assignment_to.description: Relates something (typically an assignment) to the thing the resource is assigned to, such as a project, position, organization, pay rate, or billing rate.
is_assignment_to.title: is assignment to

is_based_on.description: The object is a foundation for, a starting point for, gave rise to, or justifies the subject.
examples: A document is based on a document template; a metric computing the average income of a population is based on the metric for individual income.
is_based_on.title: is based on

is_categorized_by.description: Relates something to a taxonomy term or other less formally defined classification.
is_categorized_by.title: is categorized by

is_connected_to.description: A non-owning, non-causal, non-subordinate (i.e., peer-to-peer) relationship.
is_connected_to.title: is connected to

is_direct_part_of.description: The relationship between a part and a whole where the part has independent existence and there are no other parts in between.
is_direct_part_of.title: is direct part of

is_expressed_in.description: Relates something to the language it is expressed in.
is_expressed_in.title: is expressed in

is_governed_by.description: Relates an entity to another entity that controls, directs, determines or has a guiding influence or authority over it.
examples: A country geographic region is governed by a country government; the installation and use of software is governed by a license.
is_governed_by.title: is governed by

is_identified_by.description: Relates something to a content object that uniquely identifies it.
is_identified_by.title: is identified by

is_made_up_of.description: Relates something to a substance that it is made up of.
examples: A vase is made of clay; water is made up of hydrogen and oxygen.
is_made_up_of.title: is made up of

is_member_of.description: Relates a member individual to the thing, such as a collection or organization, that it is a member of.
is_member_of.title: is member of

is_part_of.description: The relationship between a part and a whole where the part has independent existence.
is_part_of.title: is part of

is_produced_by.description: Relates something to the thing that created, composed, or brought it into existence.
examples: A deliverable is produces by a task.
A measurement is produced by a sensor.
A painting is produced by a person.
is_produced_by.title: is produced by

is_recognized_by.description: Relates something to a party that formally acknowledges its existence, validity, or legality.
examples: The existence of a particular company is recognized by the state.
is_recognized_by.title: is recognized by

is_recorded_at.description: The date that something was posted (which is not necessarily the date it occurred). It must be after the date of occurrence, but could be before or after the planned date.
examples: The date and time a customer payment or stock purchase was posted.
is_recorded_at.title: is recorded at

is_rendered_on.description: Relates content to the media on which it is rendered.
examples: A document is rendered on a computer screen; a piece of music is rendered through speakers.
is_rendered_on.title: is rendered on

is_triggered_by.description: Relates a contingency, such as an event or obligation, to the event that gives rise to it.
examples: Fire insurance is contingent on a particular building burning down; the death benefit payout on a life insurance policy is contingent on the death of the insured person.
is_triggered_by.title: is triggered by

is_under_jurisdiction_of.description: Relates a law, contract, etc., to the system of law or government which has the power, right, or authority to interpret and apply it.
is_under_jurisdiction_of.title: is under jurisdiction of

links.description: Relates a network link to a network node that it connects to another node. Used when the connection is undirected or the direction is not known.
links.title: links

links_from.description: Relates a network link to its origin network node. Unlike the superproperty, this represents a directed connection.
links_from.title: links from

links_to.description: Relates a network link to its destination network node. Unlike the superproperty, this represents a directed connection.
links_to.title: links to

name.description: Relates an individual to (one of) its name(s).
name.title: name

numeric_value.description: The actual value of a magnitude.
numeric_value.title: numeric value

occurs_in.description: Relates something, such as an event, to the geographic location where it did, does, or will happen.
occurs_in.title: occurs in

offers_to_provide.description: Relates an offer to the thing being made available for exchange.
examples: An offer to provide a specific product in exchange for an amount of money or to pay a certain price for a home that is for sale.
offers_to_provide.title: offers to provide

offers_to_receive.description: Relates an offer to the thing expected in return for the offered item.
examples: A vendor makes an offer to receive a particular amount of money in exchange for the offered product; an offer to receive a home in exchange for an amount of money.
offers_to_receive.title: offers to receive

planned_end_date.description: The date that something is or was planned to end, with precision of one day.
planned_end_date.title: planned end date

planned_end_date_time.description: The date that something is or was planned to end, with no implied precision.
planned_end_date_time.title: planned end date time

planned_end_minute.description: The date and time that something is or was planned to end, with precision of one minute.
planned_end_minute.title: planned end minute

planned_end_year.description: The date that something is or was planned to end, with precision of one year.
examples: The automobile manufacturer announced that it will stop producing gas-powered vehicles in 2035.
planned_end_year.title: planned end year

planned_start_date.description: The date that something is or was planned to start, with precision of one day.
planned_start_date.title: planned start date

planned_start_date_time.description: The date and time that something is or was planned to start, with no implied precision.
planned_start_date_time.title: planned start date time

planned_start_minute.description: The date and time that something is or was planned to start, with precision of one minute.
planned_start_minute.title: planned start minute

planned_start_year.description: The date that something is or was planned to start, with precision of one year.
examples: The automobile manufacturer announced that its full line-up will include only electric cars starting in 2035.
planned_start_year.title: planned start year

precedes.description: A generic ordering relation indicating that the subject comes before the object.
precedes.title: precedes

precedes_directly.description: A generic ordering relation indicating that the subject comes immediately before the object.
precedes_directly.title: precedes directly

refers_to.description: Relates something to another resource that it points to, indicates, or references.
refers_to.title: refers to

requires.description: The subject needs the object or makes it necessary, mandatory, or compulsory.
examples: Humans require air; solar power requires sunshine.
requires.title: requires

sequence.description: A number that specifies the position of an element within a series.
sequence.title: sequence

start_date_time.description: The date and time that something starts.
start_date_time.title: start date time

symbol.description: A symbol for something using only ASCII characters.
examples: The ASCII symbol for square meter is m^2.
symbol.title: symbol

unique_text.description: The unique string value of some content object, to be used when there is no possibility of having more than one value.
examples: The unique string for a vehicle identification number.
unique_text.title: unique text

UnitOfMeasure.title: Unit of Measure
